analysis.title: Upgrading U.S. Treasuries to lock in income
key_insights: BlackRock upgrades U.S. Treasuries, preferring short-term bonds, because higher yields improve potential returns. The move is partly funded by downgrading U.S. equities to neutral.

Short-term Treasuries move to overweight, where the firm sees scope for excessive Fed tightening expectations to unwind. Long-term Treasuries move to neutral because higher yields now compensate better for interest-rate risk.
The 10-year Treasury yield has risen 110 basis points this year to around 5.25%. The rise is driven mainly by higher real interest rates, not inflation expectations or term premium.
Two forces lift real rates. Competition for capital is pushing up the neutral rate, and Middle East tensions and higher oil prices have sharply reversed Fed rate expectations.
Markets have priced in 160 additional basis points of Fed tightening over the next 12 months since January. BlackRock thinks this is overdone.
With term premium averaging around 75 basis points since September, BlackRock sees a 75-basis-point cushion against further yield increases over 12 months before total returns turn negative.

U.S. equities are cut from overweight to neutral as a short-term risk-management move around volatility from the AI buildout and growing focus on AI policy. BlackRock keeps its conviction in AI fundamentals and its preference for AI within U.S. equities.
BlackRock trims its Japanese government bond underweight. The underweight was held since July 2023, when 10-year yields were 0.4%-0.5%, versus above 3% now.
U.S. agency mortgage-backed securities are moved to neutral and used as a funding source for the Treasury upgrade.
Emerging market equities stay overweight, supported by strong earnings and cheaper valuations. The firm cites AI scarcity themes across Asia and Latin America.

Last week 10- and 30-year U.S. Treasury yields hit their highest levels since 2002 before retreating after strong bond auctions. European bonds also sold off, led by France on fiscal concerns, and oil rose on Middle East tensions.

U.S. CPI (Oct. 14) and PPI (Oct. 15) are the first reads on September inflation. BlackRock is watching for persistent price pressure from higher energy costs and recent PCE methodology changes, which could shift Fed expectations and Treasury yields.

Credit stance: selectivity is needed amid tight spreads. BlackRock is underweight long-term IG credit, neutral on short-term IG and global high yield, and prefers higher-rated high yield. It is overweight emerging local-currency debt.

sector_views.rationale: Downgraded from overweight to manage near-term volatility around the AI buildout and AI policy focus. AI fundamentals remain strong and AI/tech is still favored.
Strong earnings and cheaper valuations create opportunities, especially AI scarcity expressions across Asia and Latin America.
Needs more business-friendly policy and deeper capital markets to outperform. Favors financials, infrastructure and industrials.
Strong corporate balance sheets and governance reforms are supportive. Prefers physical AI and buildout bottlenecks.
Sees opportunities in physical AI. Cheap open-source AI could drive adoption without necessarily lifting AI-provider profitability.

earnings_insights: FactSet data shows third-quarter S&P 500 earnings expected to grow nearly 30% year-on-year (consensus estimate, not yet reported).

trade_ideas.description: Overweight short-term U.S. Treasuries, funded partly by U.S. agency MBS (now neutral) and U.S. equities (now neutral)
trade_ideas.rationale: Much of the anticipated repricing has occurred, and expectations for further Fed hikes look excessive at the front end.
trade_ideas.risk: Yields could keep rising as competition for capital intensifies.

trade_ideas.description: Move long-term U.S. Treasuries from underweight to neutral
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher yields now provide better compensation for interest-rate risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Room remains for yields to rise as competition for capital intensifies.

trade_ideas.description: Trim underweight in Japanese government bonds (remains underweight)
trade_ideas.rationale: Substantial repricing in yields has improved risk-reward.
trade_ideas.risk: Further rate hikes and heavy issuance could push JGB yields higher.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight emerging market local-currency debt and emerging market equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Attractive yield relative to volatility, improving fundamentals, strong earnings and cheaper valuations.

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening if inflation proves persistent from higher energy costs and PCE methodology changes.
Competition for capital could keep pushing yields higher.
Volatility around the AI buildout and AI policy uncertainty.
Heavy JGB issuance and further Bank of Japan rate hikes.
Higher energy prices could push euro area rates higher.
Political uncertainty and price-sensitive buyers add volatility risk to UK gilts.
Tight credit spreads and increased corporate issuance.
vol_and_positioning: BlackRock downgrades U.S. equities to neutral as a short-term risk-management move to manage potential volatility around the AI buildout. It says investors must be more dynamic in the current volatile macro and market regime.
Long-term Treasury yields may still rise as competition for capital intensifies, which is why long-term Treasuries are only neutral.
The front end offers a greater breakeven buffer against rate increases, which is why short-term Treasuries are favored.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions persisted and pushed oil prices higher, adding to inflation worries and driving a reversal in Fed rate expectations.
Growing focus on AI policy and the AI buildout in jurisdictions across the country is a factor in the U.S. equity downgrade.
European bonds sold off, led by France, on fiscal concerns.
Geopolitical fragmentation and strategic competition between major powers is one of five mega forces in BlackRock's framework.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price 160 basis points of extra Fed tightening, which BlackRock thinks is overdone. A 75-basis-point cushion and term premium averaging 75 basis points make short-term Treasuries attractive.
tension_points.bear_case: Competition for capital is pushing up the neutral rate, and BlackRock still sees room for yields to rise. Higher energy prices and persistent inflation could keep the Fed hawkish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot September CPI (Oct. 14) or PPI (Oct. 15) that raises Fed tightening expectations and Treasury yields further.
